Messages.Author: ThE OnLy VipeR
Messages.Body:

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
ThE OnLy VipeR wrote:
> 1.- Do I have to pay Leandro´s penalty to burn a pool and bring a new
> vampire to my uncontrolled region?

Yes. You pay your Leandro tax or you lose all your transfers. You must
spend four transfers and a pool to bring a new vampire to your
uncontrolled region from your crypt.

> 2.- If I moved Ingrid Rosler to my Ready Region, can I use the two
> extra transfers immediately?

No. Ingrid, or any other vampire with blood equal to their capacity, is
moved out of your uncontrolled region at *the end* of your influence
phase. It's too late to spend more transfers.

-Robert

couple of times. After that, GAME ON!

Messages.Author: mrjay1000
Messages.Body:
Sure it's the same. As I said in the second part of my post, some
allowances could, and SHOULD be made, especially when playing in a
friendly group, or with newbies. Remind people the first couple of
times to pay to contest. After that, it's your job to remember. By
forgetting to gain from the edge, you have chosen not to utilize it's
benefits. By forgetting to play a master card, you have chosen not to
play one. If you forget to give a vampire a blood from a Hunting
Ground, they'll just have to go a little hungry. By forgetting to pay
for contestation, you have chosen to yield.

Now don't get me wrong, I'm actually glad that the judge ruled in your
favor, though. I, personally would have allowed you to pay to contest,
especially since it was the first turn after the contestation. I may
have reminded you a second time, but the third time, I would have let
it go until your turn was over and by then it's just too damned late.
This is more than fair. It's not your job (nor anyone else's) to
police every table, all of the time, just to make sure that everyone is
remembering everything that they need to during their appropriate
phases.

Besides, in my experience with Leandro (and they have been numerous),
usually by the second time, everyone at the table has incentive to
remind someone else to "pay their Leandro Tax."

Messages.Author: Ankur Gupta
Messages.Body:
> Ground, they'll just have to go a little hungry. By forgetting to pay
> for contestation, you have chosen to yield.

Contestation *is* different as far as I know. It is a choice unlike your
other examples that requires a specific non-default answer (since no
default answer exists). Leandro is much the same. The reason is because
these are "must" decisions. They are not optional in the way that gaining
from the edge, using a hunting ground, or playing a master card are
optional. There is no default assumption that forgetting to pay suggests
yielding. I would make allowances for casual or newbie play (as would
most, I'd imagine), but in a tournament, I'd remind a player to make a
decision. Or penalize him if it's clear he's trying to gain an advantage
by maliciously "forgetting" until it's relevant each turn.

Ankur

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
mrjay1000 wrote:
> By forgetting to pay
> for contestation, you have chosen to yield.

Equivalently: By forgetting to yield, you have chosen to pay.

The resulting contradiction is yet another way to illustrate that the
choice must be made. Neither yielding nor paying to contest is a
default. The choice has no default.
